title: Don Quixote, pages 49–53
blurb: What happened in the funeral procession, and what is making the noise in the dark. About four minutes.
sub: Eight questions on tonight's reading, about four minutes. Just the story: what happened, and who it happened to.
cite: Don Quixote by Miguel de Cervantes, Core Classics abridged for young readers
note: Questions and answers are shuffled every time, so running it twice is not the same quiz twice. Get one wrong and a hint names the page.

items.q: After the fight with the shepherds, what did Sancho find was missing?
opts: The saddlebags holding their food, which the innkeeper had kept as payment.
His donkey, which had bolted when the shepherds began slinging stones.
The mule carrying their water, which had strayed off in the dark.
Rocinante's saddle and bridle, which Don Quixote had pawned at the last inn to pay for the balsam.
items.hint: Sancho went to the pouches on his donkey for something to clean his master's mouth, and got a shock instead.
items.why: He went to the pouches to clean his master's mouth and found the bags gone. The innkeeper had taken them as payment, and Sancho never noticed during his hasty exit.

items.q: How did Don Quixote explain being beaten by a flock of sheep?
opts: The sheep had been enchanted by the innkeeper who stole their bags.
He had drunk too much of the balsam and could not see straight.
His enemy the enchanter had turned the armies into flocks out of envy.
He said he had never claimed they were armies, and that Sancho had misheard every word of it.
items.hint: Sancho scolded him for meddling with what were only sheep. Don Quixote blamed the same person he always blames.
items.why: He told Sancho that the thief of an enchanter, his mortal enemy, envies the glory he would gain from battle, and so transforms armies into flocks.

items.q: What did the moving lights on the road turn out to be?
opts: A band of enchanted Moors on their way to the nearest inn.
A throng of figures dressed in white, carrying a black litter.
Shepherds with torches, out looking for the sheep that had scattered.
Mule drivers taking lanterns down to the inn where the blanket-tossers were waiting.
items.hint: Look again at what the figures were wearing on page 50, and at what they carried between them.
items.why: A vast throng dressed in white carried a black litter in their midst. Sancho hid at the side of the road while Don Quixote held his ground.

items.q: How did the man in white end up on the ground with a broken leg?
opts: Don Quixote ran him through with the lance as he tried to push past.
He fell while trying to lift the black litter down off its poles.
Sancho jumped out from the roadside and pulled him down by his white robe.
Don Quixote seized his mule's bridle and the mule reared and threw him.
items.hint: The lance never touched him. Look at what Don Quixote grabbed when the man tried to push past.
items.why: The man tried to push past, so Don Quixote grabbed the bridle; the mule reared on its hind legs and threw its rider to the ground.

items.q: Who were the white figures really, and what were they carrying?
opts: Friars taking the bones of a saint from Baeza back to La Mancha.
Masqueraders on their way home from a carnival in the next village.
Brothers in Holy Orders, escorting a dead gentleman's body to Segovia.
Mourners from Segovia carrying a knight who had been killed in a duel on the road to Baeza.
items.hint: The man Don Quixote knocked down told him where they had set out from and where the casket was going.
items.why: They had come from Baeza to escort a casket holding the body of a gentleman they were taking to Segovia, his birthplace, for burial.

items.q: Why was Don Quixote disappointed by what the man told him?
opts: The gentleman had died of a fever, so there was no wrong to set right.
The man refused to name the knight who had killed the gentleman.
The brothers had no food or wine with them that he could ask for.
The man would not swear that Dulcinea del Toboso was the most beautiful lady in the world.
items.hint: He asked who had killed the man. The answer left him nothing to avenge.
items.why: He asked who killed the gentleman and was told: God, by a fever. Nobody had done a wrong, and righting wrongs is his business.

items.q: What sounds stopped the two of them in the dark valley?
opts: Trumpets and drums, the same ones he had heard out on the dusty plain.
The bleating of sheep somewhere further up among the lofty trees.
Many voices whispering together, which Sancho took for the spirits of the dead.
Falling water, and heavy blows with clanging iron and rattling chains.
items.hint: They set out looking for water. They found the sound of it, and something else sounding underneath it.
items.why: Hunting for a spring, they heard falling waters, and then heavy blows at regular intervals with the clanging of iron and the rattling of chains. They could not understand the noise.

items.q: What did Don Quixote tell Sancho to do before riding into the glen?
opts: Follow him in at a distance, carrying the lance and the shield.
Wait three days, then go home to the village and on to Toboso.
Ride straight for the inn and bring back help before midnight.
Go back to the funeral procession and beg the brothers for wine and water.
items.hint: He gave Sancho a number of days to wait, and two places to go to if he never came back.
items.why: His final instruction was to wait three days; if he had not returned by then, Sancho was to go home to their village and then to Toboso.
